false_positives.candidate:
Uses Python 3.13-only queue shutdown APIs

OrderedQueueWorker catches queue.ShutDown (also at line 142) and FixedQueuePool.shutdown calls Queue.shutdown(immediate=False) at line 238. queue.ShutDown and Queue.shutdown were added in Python 3.13. If this consumer runs on an older Python interpreter supported by Sentry, attribute resolution or the shutdown call will fail at runtime, breaking worker exception handling and/or graceful shutdown. This needs a compatibility fallback or an explicit Python 3.13+ requirement.

Strategy.close shuts down a shared queue pool that may be reused after rebalance

ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool per factory (result_consumer.py line 133) and passes that same pool to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy (result_consumer.py line 254). SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close shuts down the pool. Arroyo can close a strategy on partition revocation/rebalance and later create a new strategy from the same factory. After the first close, the pool's queues and worker threads are permanently shut down, so later submissions will fail and be treated as completed, allowing unprocessed messages to be committed.

Shutdown does not drain queues and can drop pending work

FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown = True before draining queues, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join/close never waits for wait_until_empty. Workers therefore stop after their current item, leaving queued WorkItems unprocessed. OrderedQueueWorker also never calls work_queue.task_done(), so any shutdown/join path that depends on unfinished tasks cannot complete correctly. On consumer shutdown, queued messages can be discarded and completed offsets may not be committed.

OffsetTracker iterates all_offsets keys while other threads mutate it

get_committable_offsets builds list(self.all_offsets.keys()) without a global lock while submit()/add_offset() can concurrently insert new Partition keys. This can raise RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration. The commit loop catches the exception, but that iteration's commits are skipped, which can delay offset commits during partition churn.

Work queues are unbounded, providing no backpressure

FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize and submit() uses put() unconditionally. If workers are slower than incoming Kafka messages (for example due to a slow subscription), the consumer will continue polling and queueing decoded WorkItems without bound, retaining both decoded results and original messages. This can exhaust memory; the claimed 'natural backpressure' does not exist.

Offsets are completed even when processing fails

OrderedQueueWorker calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in a finally block even when result_processor raises. ResultProcessor.__call__ also swallows handling exceptions. Therefore a message that fails handling (for example a transient DB error) is treated as done and becomes committable. The consumer will commit past it and never retry it, despite the strategy's documentation saying offsets are committed only after successful processing.

submit() marks failed submissions as completed, allowing unprocessed offsets to commit

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit catches all exceptions and, when broker metadata is present, adds and immediately completes the offset. If queue_pool.submit fails (for example because the queue is shut down, the pool is in a bad state, or an unexpected error occurs before enqueue), the message is never processed but is still considered complete, so the commit loop may commit it and silently lose the result.

Committable-offset calculation scans integer ranges and sets repeatedly

Every commit-loop iteration computes min(all_offsets) and max(all_offsets) for each partition and then loops over every integer from start to max_offset. With large batches, many outstanding offsets, or a stuck offset, this can become CPU-intensive. The per-partition offset sets also grow until a contiguous prefix can be committed, increasing memory pressure during backlogs.

join() ignores its timeout and does not flush pending work

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join(timeout) simply calls close(), which stops the commit thread with a fixed 5-second join and shuts down the pool without waiting for queued items or honoring the supplied timeout. Arroyo's join contract is to allow pending processing to finish up to the timeout; this implementation can terminate early and leave work unprocessed/uncommitted.

Hash-distribution test is nondeterministic

test_different_groups_distributed asserts that 20 hashed group names hit all three queues. Python's randomized string hashing does not guarantee that every bucket is hit for this small sample, so the test can fail intermittently. It should use a deterministic hash function or only assert consistent assignment.

Negative --max-workers creates an invalid queue pool

For thread-queue-parallel mode, num_queues is set to max_workers or 20. A negative max_workers value is truthy, so FixedQueuePool receives a negative num_queues; range(num_queues) creates no queues and hash(group_key) % negative_num_queues can produce invalid indices. The CLI option should validate that max_workers is positive.

Using login can cause legitimate installs to fail after renames and may allow a different account that acquired an old login to pass this ownership check. Compare stable IDs instead.

Installation ownership is not validated when the Integration row does not exist

If Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist, GitHubInstallation.dispatch immediately calls pipeline.next_step(), which leads build_integration to create the integration using only the supplied installation_id. In that path the newly added github_authenticated_user check is never applied because there is no sender metadata. If the GitHub webhook is delayed or fails, or if an attacker knows or guesses an installation_id that has not yet been recorded, a user who completed GitHub OAuth as any GitHub account may be able to attach that GitHub installation to their own Sentry organization. This path should fail closed or verify ownership before creating the integration.

User info lookup failures are not handled gracefully

get_user_info(payload['access_token']) is called without exception handling. If GitHub's user endpoint returns an error, times out, rate-limits the request, or otherwise fails after the token exchange, the pipeline dispatch will raise and likely produce a 500. Since this PR is meant to present a controlled failure page for invalid installation requests, this call should catch integration/API errors and return error().

OAuth authorize URL parameters are not URL-encoded

The redirect to GitHub's OAuth authorize endpoint is built by string interpolation without URL-encoding the query parameters. redirect_uri in particular should be form-url-encoded; if absolute_uri ever includes special characters, query components, or non-ASCII characters, the authorize request may be malformed or rejected. Use urlencode to build the query string.

Empty installation_id query parameter is treated as present

GitHubInstallation.dispatch uses request.GET.get('installation_id', pipeline.fetch_state('installation_id')) and then only checks installation_id is None. A request with installation_id= will bind an empty string and continue the pipeline instead of falling back to the stored state or redirecting to the app URL. This can lead to a confusing downstream failure when build_integration is called with an empty installation ID. Treat empty values as missing.

Direct GitHub install redirect does not validate installation_id

When provider_id is github and setup_action=install but no pipeline exists, the code reads installation_id from the query string and passes it directly to reverse(). If installation_id is missing, this can generate an invalid redirect or raise an exception depending on URL resolver behavior. Validate that installation_id is present before redirecting, or redirect to a safe default installation flow.

Security tests do not cover the main identity-validation edge cases

test_github_user_mismatch only exercises a login-string mismatch where webhook sender metadata exists. It does not cover missing sender metadata, stable GitHub user ID comparison, renamed/reclaimed logins, or the path where Integration.DoesNotExist skips ownership validation and proceeds to build_integration. Because this PR is a security fix, these edge cases should have explicit tests.

In Create, the goroutine derives a 10-second context from the incoming request context with context.WithTimeoutCause. Because Create returns immediately, the HTTP request context is canceled when the request completes, canceling the child context and likely abortting Legacy.Create. The same pattern is used in Delete (line 110), Update (line 135), and DeleteCollection (line 163). This defeats the purpose of the asynchronous legacy safety write. Rapid create/update/delete requests for the same object can cause legacy operations to run out of order, for example update before create, delete before create, or create after delete. This can leave the legacy store inconsistent even though unified storage is correct. Since mode 3 is intended to keep legacy as a safe fallback, these writes need per-resource ordering or another synchronization mechanism.

The previous implementation precomputed the updated object and passed the unified result to legacy. The new code can write a different object to legacy than the one stored in unified storage. Legacy delete is skipped when unified delete returns NotFound

The previous mode 3 behavior tolerated NotFound from unified storage and still attempted Legacy.Delete, allowing cleanup of stale legacy objects. With this change, an object that exists only in legacy will not be removed, leaving orphaned data in the legacy store even though the API returns NotFound.

Storage failures are recorded as legacy duration metrics

In Create, when Storage.Create fails, the code calls recordLegacyDuration with the storage start time. The same happens in Update at line 129. This attributes unified-storage latency and errors to the legacy store and fails to record a storage duration for the failed storage operation. Metrics and alerts for legacy and storage error rates will be incorrect.

Asynchronous legacy write failures are not logged

The goroutines for Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection only record a metric when the legacy operation fails; they do not log the error or identify the affected object. Since the API returns success to the client even if the legacy safety write fails, operators have little information to detect or diagnose divergence. DualWriterMode3.Destroy destroys both Storage and Legacy immediately, but write methods launch untracked goroutines that may still be using Legacy. In a flex row, floats on flex items are ignored and non-growing items do not fill the remaining width, so the button may no longer be pushed to the right edge as in the previous float/block layout.

In addition, website_name is derived from website, which is listed in untrusted_attributes, but website_name itself is not treated as untrusted. true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same bug: calling `i.content.scrub` when `i.content` is nil (because RSS feeds often lack a `content` element) will cause a crash/NoMethodError.

false_positives.candidate:
External embed content is stored and rendered as raw HTML

TopicEmbed.import creates posts with skip_validations and cook_method set to Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]. Content imported from RSS/Atom feeds or remote pages is not sanitized before storage, and Post#cook returns the raw HTML for this cook method. This allows untrusted external HTML, including scripts and dangerous markup, to be stored and later rendered in Discourse pages.

NoMethodError when embed_by_username is blank

TopicRetriever#fetch_http calls SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without checking whether the setting is present. If embed_by_username is blank, this raises NoMethodError. This can happen when embedding is partially configured: embeddable_host is set, but no import username has been chosen.

Host validation does not reject a blank embeddable host

TopicRetriever#invalid_host? compares SiteSetting.embeddable_host with the URI host. If embeddable_host is blank and the parsed URI also has a nil host, the method returns false instead of treating the URL as invalid. The retriever should explicitly reject retrieval when no embeddable host is configured.

Redis throttle key can be left without expiry

retrieved_recently? uses $redis.setnx followed by $redis.expire. If the process crashes or the expire call fails between these two operations, the Redis key remains forever without a TTL, permanently throttling retrieval for that embed URL. An atomic SET with NX and expiry should be used.

Embed retrieval runs the entire feed poll synchronously

When feed polling is enabled, TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve instantiates Jobs::PollFeed and executes it synchronously just to see whether one embed URL appears in the feed. This imports every item in the configured feed, which can be expensive and can create many unrelated topics during a single embed request.

Readability import allows href/src without scheme sanitization

import_remote uses ruby-readability with an allow-list that includes a and img tags and href/src attributes, but it does not sanitize attribute URL schemes. Dangerous URLs such as javascript: links can survive and be stored in the post. Since imported posts are rendered as raw HTML, this creates an XSS risk.

Failed post creation can still attempt TopicEmbed creation

After PostCreator#create returns, TopicEmbed.import checks post.present? before creating the TopicEmbed record. PostCreator can return an unsaved post object after a rollback, for example when host spam detection triggers. In that case post.present? is true but post.id/topic_id are nil, so TopicEmbed.create! will fail or raise a database error. The code should check that the post was persisted.

Updating an embed crashes if the post was deleted

When an existing TopicEmbed is found, the update path uses embed.post without verifying that the post still exists. If the embedded topic or post has been deleted, embed.post is nil and PostRevisor.new(post) will raise. Feed polling or retrieval for that URL will then repeatedly fail.

content_sha1 is updated even if the revision fails

TopicEmbed.import updates embed.content_sha1 immediately after calling PostRevisor#revise!, without checking whether the revision succeeded. If the post cannot be saved, the stored SHA1 will no longer match the post contents, and future legitimate content changes may be skipped because the embed record believes it is already up to date.

URL absolutizer mishandles protocol-relative and relative URLs

absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src values that start with '/'. Protocol-relative URLs such as '//cdn.example.com/x' are also matched and incorrectly rewritten to the current host, and ordinary relative URLs such as 'page.html' are left unchanged. This can break links and images in imported content.

PostCreator accepts arbitrary cook_method without validation

PostCreator now assigns post.cook_method from @opts[:cook_method] without validating the value or restricting which callers may use raw_html. Since the raw_html cook method bypasses the normal sanitization pipeline, exposing or forwarding this option accidentally could allow unsafe HTML to be stored.

Embed iframe URL assumes discourseUrl has a trailing slash

embed.js builds the iframe src as discourseUrl + 'embed/best?...'. If discourseUrl is provided without a trailing slash, the resulting URL becomes invalid, for example 'https://forum.example.comembed/best'. The script should normalize discourseUrl or insert a slash when missing.

Embed script crashes if target element is missing

The embed script calls comments.appendChild(iframe) after document.getElementById('discourse-comments'). If the host page does not contain an element with id discourse-comments, comments is null and the script throws a TypeError, preventing any further script execution.

Migration uses force: true and can drop existing data

CreateTopicEmbeds creates the topic_embeds table with force: true. In a migration this will drop the table if it already exists, destroying any existing topic embed records. Migrations should not use force: true unless intentional data loss is explicitly desired.

Unrelated migration changed to force table recreation

This PR modifies the existing create_top_topics migration to use force: true. That change is unrelated to embed handling and can drop an existing top_topics table, losing data if the table already exists in an environment where this migration is applied or reapplied.

Feed fetch has no timeouts

PollFeed uses open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without configuring connect/read timeouts. A slow or unresponsive feed can hang the job and occupy a Sidekiq worker indefinitely.

Controller spec does not test the enqueued job

The spec expects TopicRetriever to be instantiated and retrieve directly, but EmbedController#best enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic instead. The test therefore does not verify the actual behavior of the controller unless jobs are executed inline, and it does not assert the job arguments.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

Existing callers using downsize(from, to, width, height) will now have height interpreted as opts, or will raise ArgumentError if an options hash is also supplied. The command will fail, so large animated GIFs will not be downsized and the loop will either retry uselessly or proceed with an oversized file.

false_positives.candidate:
413 error message reports a hardcoded 10MB limit

displayErrorForUpload now tells the user that the maximum upload size is 10MB after a 413 response, regardless of the actual site setting or web server limit. This can display an incorrect maximum size to the user.

URL downloads ignore configured upload size limits

FileHelper.download was changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a fixed 10.megabytes for all URL-based API uploads. This ignores both max_image_size_kb and any attachment size limit, allowing the server to download up to 10MB even when the configured limit is lower.

In-place downsizing can corrupt or destroy the uploaded tempfile

The loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) and ignores the return value. If the conversion or optimization fails, truncates the file, or produces a corrupt image, the original uploaded data has already been overwritten and the controller may continue to Upload.create_for with a damaged or zero-byte file. A separate output file and explicit failure handling are needed.

Automatic downsizing is attempted for vector images such as SVG

The condition uses FileHelper.is_image?(filename), which treats SVG as an image elsewhere in Discourse. OptimizedImage.downsize is a raster ImageMagick resize and cannot meaningfully or safely reduce an SVG file in place. Large SVG uploads will repeatedly fail downsizing or may be corrupted before upload; vector formats should be excluded or handled separately.

No tests cover the new automatic downsizing behavior

There are no tests for the new server-side downsizing loop, including oversized images, failed conversions, animated GIFs, SVGs, or interaction with configured size limits. These cases are likely to regress and are risky areas of this change.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists

TopicsController#unsubscribe does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then dereferences `tu.notification_level`. For users without an existing topic_users row for the topic, `tu` is nil and the action raises NoMethodError. The action should create or update the row, for example via TopicUser.change or find_or_create_by.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the exact same bug: `tu` can be nil when no `TopicUser` record exists, leading to a crash (NoMethodError / nil pointer exception) when calling methods on `tu`.

false_positives.candidate:
State-changing unsubscribe action is a GET route without CSRF/token

The unsubscribe action changes TopicUser.notification_level in response to a GET request and skips XHR checks. Rails CSRF protection does not apply to GET, so any logged-in user visiting a malicious page could have topics silently muted or downgraded by an image or link to /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe. Email unsubscribe links should use a signed one-time key or a POST route.

Direct TopicUser#save! bypasses notification-level bookkeeping

The unsubscribe action mutates notification_level with `tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change`. This skips setting notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id and does not publish the MessageBus level-change event. Leaving notifications_reason_id nil can allow later automatic tracking to override the user's mute, and open clients will not receive the state change.

Global unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for all callers

The `unsubscribe_link` translation was changed to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but Email::MessageBuilder only has that value when the caller passes `unsubscribe_url`. Only `send_notification_email` was updated. Any other email or plugin that builds with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but omits `unsubscribe_url` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send.

track_visit! uses topic id as user_id when passed ids

In `TopicUser.track_visit!`, `user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic` falls back to the `topic` argument rather than the `user` argument when the second argument is not a User object. TopicsController calls this with integer topic_id/user_id, so it can create or update topic_users rows with user_id equal to the topic_id, corrupting per-user topic state. The fallback should be `user`.

Spec does not assert the new unsubscribe_url is included

The updated spec passes `unsubscribe_url` to Email::MessageBuilder but only asserts that the body contains `user_preferences_url`. It never checks that the new per-topic unsubscribe URL appears in the body or HTML, so the new interpolation/link behavior is untested.

true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same problem: throwing a generic/plain Error for auth failures instead of a structured TRPCError (such as FORBIDDEN), which causes tRPC to treat it as an internal server error (500).

true_positives.golden_comment: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

The cache last-updated timestamp is formatted using Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US') regardless of the user's locale. This ignores localized date preferences and can show an English/US-formatted timestamp to non-English users.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the exact same issue: a date/timestamp is being formatted with a hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of respecting the user's locale.

false_positives.candidate:
Delete-cache mutation does not refresh connected calendars

The deleteCache mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback. It does not invalidate or refetch viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike the disconnect mutation. Since SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper displays cache status from that query and may not provide an onChanged handler that invalidates it, the UI can keep showing the old cache status and timestamp after cache deletion succeeds.

getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns the maximum updatedAt for CalendarCache rows without filtering by expiresAt, while getCachedAvailability only treats rows with expiresAt >= now as valid. As a result, connectedCalendars can report cacheUpdatedAt and show cache actions for credentials whose cache entries are expired, misleading users about whether valid cached data exists.

The wrapper computes shouldDisableConnectionModification as isDisabled || disableConnectionModification, but ConnectedCalendarList receives only disableConnectionModification. When disabledScope matches the current scope, calendar switches are disabled, but CredentialActionsDropdown can still allow deleting cache or disconnecting the integration, defeating the disabled-scope restriction.

Empty actions container is rendered when dropdown is hidden

The actions prop always renders a fixed-width div around CredentialActionsDropdown. When the dropdown returns null, such as for delegation credentials with no cache or when connection modification is disabled, the empty container remains and creates unnecessary blank space in the list item or alert action area.

dev:cron uses npx tsx without declaring tsx

The dev:cron script was changed to npx tsx cron-tester.ts, but tsx is not listed as a devDependency. npx may download or prompt to install tsx at runtime, making the script network-dependent and less reproducible across environments.

No automated tests for cache deletion authorization/status

There are no automated tests for the new deleteCache handler's ownership check, the cache deletion behavior, or the connectedCalendars cache-status enrichment. These paths affect authorization and user-visible data, and regressions could go unnoticed without coverage.

This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hours end boundary uses slot start time

The variable end is calculated from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime. The check therefore ignores the event duration when validating the end of working hours. A slot that starts inside working hours but ends after endTime will pass, potentially offering slots beyond a host's working hours.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue directly states that the end variable is calculated from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, which is an exact match with the golden comment.

Dayjs objects are compared with strict equality

The check comparing date.start and date.end uses === between two Dayjs objects. This compares object identity, not timestamp, so it is always false. The intended handling of a zero-length override where start equals end never triggers. Use .isSame() instead.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the exact same bug: using strict equality (===) to compare two Dayjs objects (date.start and date.end) instead of using the .isSame() method, which causes the comparison to always evaluate to false.

false_positives.candidate:
Date override short-circuits busy-time check

In checkIfIsAvailable, when a date override exists for the day, the function returns true before running the busy.every overlap check. Any calendar busy time or existing booking during the override is ignored, so slots can be offered even though the host is busy. This can cause double bookings, especially for fixed hosts whose availability must block the whole event.

Date override validation allows partially overlapping slots

The override exclusion only tests whether the slot ends before the override starts or starts after the override ends. It does not test whether the slot starts before the override or ends after it. Therefore a slot that only partially overlaps the override is treated as inside it. For fixed hosts, a slot such as 09:30-10:30 can pass even if the host override is only 10:00-11:00.

Working-hours check accepts slots when no working hours cover the day

The new workingHours validation only rejects a slot if it finds a workingHours entry for the slot weekday and the slot is outside that entry. If the host has no workingHours entry for that weekday, or workingHours is empty, find returns undefined and the host is treated as available subject only to busy times. This allows fixed hosts to be booked on days they have no scheduled availability.

Multiple date overrides on the same day make valid slots unavailable

The date override loop marks the slot as outside if it is outside any override on that date. If a user has two overrides on the same day, a slot inside one override is outside the other, causing dateOverrides.find to return true and checkIfIsAvailable to return false. The logic should accept a slot if it is contained in at least one override.

Multiple working-hour intervals are handled incorrectly

workingHours.find returns true when the slot is outside any single working-hours interval. If a user has split working hours, such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, a valid slot in one interval is outside the other, so the slot is rejected. The code should accept a slot if it fits in at least one interval.

Date override date matching is not done in UTC

dayjs(date.start).add(...) creates a local-mode Dayjs, while slotStartTime is explicitly UTC. The YYYY MM DD comparison therefore depends on the server's local timezone and can mismatch near date boundaries. The adjusted override times should be constructed in UTC before formatting and comparing.

Timezone-converted overrides can wrap to another day without handling

After applying the invitee/organizer offset, start and end minutes are derived from hour() and minute(), which wrap at midnight. If the timezone conversion moves an override into the previous or next local day, the code still assigns those minutes to the current invitee day, which can drop the override or place slots on the wrong day. Converted ranges that cross midnight need to be split or filtered by the resulting date.

Missing tests for fixed-host round-robin override behavior

The added test only checks a personal event with a different attendee timezone. The PR description says it fixes round-robin events with fixed hosts and date overrides, but there is no test asserting that a fixed host's date override restricts round-robin slots, nor that busy times inside an override remain unavailable. Those regressions are not covered.

In addition, all providers are instantiated before selection, so constructors that register JCA security providers run even for ignored providers. This can silently select a non-FIPS provider in a FIPS deployment or leave multiple security providers registered, breaking the previous fail-fast guarantee and creating a security/compliance risk.

Oversized ECDSA integers are truncated instead of rejected

In AuthzClientCryptoProvider's ECDSA converter, integerToBytes truncates any BigInteger whose byte array is longer than qLength by copying only the last qLength bytes. For a valid ECDSA signature, r and s must not be larger than the coordinate size, allowing at most one leading zero byte. Silently truncating oversized DER integers accepts malformed signatures and changes the numeric value, which can create signature malleability or unexpected verification behavior. The method should reject values that do not fit and should also reject negative integers.

ASN.1 sequence parsing is too lenient and can ignore malformed or trailing data

ASN1Decoder.readSequence does not validate that the declared SEQUENCE length is exactly consumed. If a child TLV is longer than the remaining sequence length, the remaining length becomes negative and parsing stops without error. If trailing bytes exist after the SEQUENCE, they are ignored because asn1derToConcatenatedRS only reads the first sequence. This lenient DER parsing can accept malformed or appended signature bytes. It should reject non-zero remaining length, child lengths that exceed the sequence, and unconsumed trailing input.

concatenatedRSToASN1DER does not validate input signature length

concatenatedRSToASN1DER assumes the supplied concatenated signature has exactly signLength bytes. It does not validate signature.length before System.arraycopy. A shorter array causes ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, while a longer array silently ignores trailing bytes. Cryptographic conversion should require the exact expected length to avoid crashes and malformed-signature acceptance.

ECDSA conversion test does not use the expected curves or verify signatures

ECDSAAlgorithmTest generates a default EC key pair and only asserts that concatenated R/S bytes are stable across conversion. It does not initialize the generator with the curves associated with ES256, ES384, and ES512, does not verify the reconstructed DER signature with the public key, and does not cover edge cases such as r/s values with the high bit set, leading zeros, extreme values, or malformed DER. false_positives.candidate:
Negative flusher_processes silently creates no flusher processes

The --flusher-processes option is not validated as positive. If a negative value is supplied, SpanFlusher computes a negative num_processes, so range(num_processes) creates no process-to-shard map entries, no flusher processes, and self.buffers is empty. The consumer will still forward/commit messages, while flusher backpressure and Redis memory checks in submit() are skipped because there are no buffers. Validate or clamp flusher_processes to a positive value before constructing SpanFlusher.

join() treats timeout=0 as no timeout

join() computes deadline as time.time() + timeout if timeout else None. A timeout of 0 is falsy, so it is treated as no timeout and join can block indefinitely even though the caller requested a non-blocking join. Use `if timeout is not None` when computing the deadline.

Flusher process health is only checked on submit

_ensure_processes_alive() is only invoked from submit(). If the consumer is idle or not receiving new span batches, poll() will not detect or restart a crashed or hung flusher process, so already-buffered segments may remain unflushed until traffic arrives. Consider checking process health in poll() or another periodic hook.

Kafka producer is not closed when the flusher loop raises

In SpanFlusher.main, producer.close() is only reached if the loop terminates normally. If produce(), future.result(), or buffer.done_flush_segments() raises, the Kafka producer is not closed before the process exits or is restarted, leaking connections/file descriptors. Close the producer in a finally block.

Unhealthy flusher process is replaced without joining/closing it

When _ensure_processes_alive() kills an unhealthy process, it immediately starts a replacement without joining or closing the old process object. This can leave zombie processes/file descriptors and creates a short window where the old and replacement processes may both act on the same shards. Join/close the killed process, with a timeout if needed, before replacing it.

OrderedQueueWorker catches queue.ShutDown (also at line 142) and FixedQueuePool.shutdown calls Queue.shutdown(immediate=False) at line 238. queue.ShutDown and Queue.shutdown were added in Python 3.13. If this consumer runs on an older Python interpreter supported by Sentry, attribute resolution or the shutdown call will fail at runtime, breaking worker exception handling and/or graceful shutdown. Strategy.close shuts down a shared queue pool that may be reused after rebalance

ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool per factory (result_consumer.py line 133) and passes that same pool to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy (result_consumer.py line 254). SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close shuts down the pool. Arroyo can close a strategy on partition revocation/rebalance and later create a new strategy from the same factory. After the first close, the pool's queues and worker threads are permanently shut down, so later submissions will fail and be treated as completed, allowing unprocessed messages to be committed.

Shutdown does not drain queues and can drop pending work

FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown = True before draining queues, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join/close never waits for wait_until_empty. Workers therefore stop after their current item, leaving queued WorkItems unprocessed. OrderedQueueWorker also never calls work_queue.task_done(), so any shutdown/join path that depends on unfinished tasks cannot complete correctly. On consumer shutdown, queued messages can be discarded and completed offsets may not be committed.

OffsetTracker iterates all_offsets keys while other threads mutate it

get_committable_offsets builds list(self.all_offsets.keys()) without a global lock while submit()/add_offset() can concurrently insert new Partition keys. This can raise RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration. The commit loop catches the exception, but that iteration's commits are skipped, which can delay offset commits during partition churn.

Work queues are unbounded, providing no backpressure

FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize and submit() uses put() unconditionally. If workers are slower than incoming Kafka messages (for example due to a slow subscription), the consumer will continue polling and queueing decoded WorkItems without bound, retaining both decoded results and original messages. This can exhaust memory; the claimed 'natural backpressure' does not exist.

Offsets are completed even when processing fails

OrderedQueueWorker calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in a finally block even when result_processor raises. ResultProcessor.__call__ also swallows handling exceptions. Therefore a message that fails handling (for example a transient DB error) is treated as done and becomes committable. The consumer will commit past it and never retry it, despite the strategy's documentation saying offsets are committed only after successful processing.

submit() marks failed submissions as completed, allowing unprocessed offsets to commit

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit catches all exceptions and, when broker metadata is present, adds and immediately completes the offset. If queue_pool.submit fails (for example because the queue is shut down, the pool is in a bad state, or an unexpected error occurs before enqueue), the message is never processed but is still considered complete, so the commit loop may commit it and silently lose the result.

Committable-offset calculation scans integer ranges and sets repeatedly

Every commit-loop iteration computes min(all_offsets) and max(all_offsets) for each partition and then loops over every integer from start to max_offset. With large batches, many outstanding offsets, or a stuck offset, this can become CPU-intensive. The per-partition offset sets also grow until a contiguous prefix can be committed, increasing memory pressure during backlogs.

join() ignores its timeout and does not flush pending work

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join(timeout) simply calls close(), which stops the commit thread with a fixed 5-second join and shuts down the pool without waiting for queued items or honoring the supplied timeout. Arroyo's join contract is to allow pending processing to finish up to the timeout; this implementation can terminate early and leave work unprocessed/uncommitted.

test_different_groups_distributed asserts that 20 hashed group names hit all three queues. Python's randomized string hashing does not guarantee that every bucket is hit for this small sample, so the test can fail intermittently. It should use a deterministic hash function or only assert consistent assignment.

For thread-queue-parallel mode, num_queues is set to max_workers or 20. A negative max_workers value is truthy, so FixedQueuePool receives a negative num_queues; range(num_queues) creates no queues and hash(group_key) % negative_num_queues can produce invalid indices. In Create, the goroutine derives a 10-second context from the incoming request context with context.WithTimeoutCause. Because Create returns immediately, the HTTP request context is canceled when the request completes, canceling the child context and likely abortting Legacy.Create. The same pattern is used in Delete (line 110), Update (line 135), and DeleteCollection (line 163). This defeats the purpose of the asynchronous legacy safety write. Use a detached context, such as context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or a background context carrying only needed values, plus the timeout.

Fire-and-forget legacy writes are not ordered

All write operations start an independent goroutine to write to legacy and do not sequence those writes. Rapid create/update/delete requests for the same object can cause legacy operations to run out of order, for example update before create, delete before create, or create after delete. This can leave the legacy store inconsistent even though unified storage is correct. Since mode 3 is intended to keep legacy as a safe fallback, these writes need per-resource ordering or another synchronization mechanism.

Async legacy create may use the same runtime.Object that is returned to the client

Create launches Legacy.Create in a goroutine with the same obj that was passed to Storage.Create. If Storage.Create mutates obj or returns it as created, the API server may serialize the returned object concurrently while the goroutine reads or mutates the same runtime.Object in Legacy.Create. runtime.Object instances are not generally safe for concurrent use. Legacy update is recomputed from objInfo instead of mirroring the unified-storage result

In Update, after Storage.Update succeeds, the async Legacy.Update is called with the original rest.UpdatedObjectInfo. Legacy.Update will typically fetch the current legacy object and call UpdatedObject again, so the legacy object may be computed from divergent legacy state or from a request-scoped or non-idempotent UpdatedObjectInfo. The previous implementation precomputed the updated object and passed the unified result to legacy. The new code can write a different object to legacy than the one stored in unified storage. Pass an UpdatedObjectInfo that returns the object returned by Storage.Update, preferably a deep copy.

Legacy delete is skipped when unified delete returns NotFound

Delete returns immediately for any Storage.Delete error, including NotFound. The previous mode 3 behavior tolerated NotFound from unified storage and still attempted Legacy.Delete, allowing cleanup of stale legacy objects. With this change, an object that exists only in legacy will not be removed, leaving orphaned data in the legacy store even though the API returns NotFound.

Storage failures are recorded as legacy duration metrics

In Create, when Storage.Create fails, the code calls recordLegacyDuration with the storage start time. The same happens in Update at line 129. This attributes unified-storage latency and errors to the legacy store and fails to record a storage duration for the failed storage operation. Metrics and alerts for legacy and storage error rates will be incorrect.

DeleteCollection records legacy async duration as a storage metric

In DeleteCollection's goroutine, after Legacy.DeleteCollection completes, the code calls recordStorageDuration. This records the legacy store's async duration and error state as if it were unified storage. Legacy failures will be invisible as legacy failures and storage metrics will be double-counted or incorrectly marked failed. This should call recordLegacyDuration.

Asynchronous legacy write failures are not logged

The goroutines for Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection only record a metric when the legacy operation fails; they do not log the error or identify the affected object. Since the API returns success to the client even if the legacy safety write fails, operators have little information to detect or diagnose divergence. DualWriterMode3.Destroy destroys both Storage and Legacy immediately, but write methods launch untracked goroutines that may still be using Legacy. On shutdown or mode change, those goroutines may fail or panic because the underlying storage has been closed. Track pending asynchronous writes and wait or cancel them during Destroy.

In addition, website_name is derived from website, which is listed in untrusted_attributes, but website_name itself is not treated as untrusted. true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. PollFeed calls i.content.scrub for every feed item. Many RSS/Atom items may not have a content element, in which case i.content is nil and nil.scrub raises NoMethodError. The scheduled job will abort and no further items in the feed will be processed.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: calling i.content.scrub when a feed item lacks content causes a nil-related exception. The candidate matches the underlying issue even though it does not suggest falling back to description.

false_positives.candidate:
External embed content is stored and rendered as raw HTML

TopicEmbed.import creates posts with skip_validations and cook_method set to Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]. Content imported from RSS/Atom feeds or remote pages is not sanitized before storage, and Post#cook returns the raw HTML for this cook method. This allows untrusted external HTML, including scripts and dangerous markup, to be stored and later rendered in Discourse pages.

NoMethodError when embed_by_username is blank

TopicRetriever#fetch_http calls SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without checking whether the setting is present. If embed_by_username is blank, this raises NoMethodError. This can happen when embedding is partially configured: embeddable_host is set, but no import username has been chosen.

Host validation does not reject a blank embeddable host

TopicRetriever#invalid_host? compares SiteSetting.embeddable_host with the URI host. If embeddable_host is blank and the parsed URI also has a nil host, the method returns false instead of treating the URL as invalid. The retriever should explicitly reject retrieval when no embeddable host is configured.

Redis throttle key can be left without expiry

retrieved_recently? uses $redis.setnx followed by $redis.expire. If the process crashes or the expire call fails between these two operations, the Redis key remains forever without a TTL, permanently throttling retrieval for that embed URL. An atomic SET with NX and expiry should be used.

Embed retrieval runs the entire feed poll synchronously

When feed polling is enabled, TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve instantiates Jobs::PollFeed and executes it synchronously just to see whether one embed URL appears in the feed. This imports every item in the configured feed, which can be expensive and can create many unrelated topics during a single embed request.

Readability import allows href/src without scheme sanitization

import_remote uses ruby-readability with an allow-list that includes a and img tags and href/src attributes, but it does not sanitize attribute URL schemes. Dangerous URLs such as javascript: links can survive and be stored in the post. Since imported posts are rendered as raw HTML, this creates an XSS risk.

Failed post creation can still attempt TopicEmbed creation

After PostCreator#create returns, TopicEmbed.import checks post.present? before creating the TopicEmbed record. PostCreator can return an unsaved post object after a rollback, for example when host spam detection triggers. In that case post.present? is true but post.id/topic_id are nil, so TopicEmbed.create! will fail or raise a database error. The code should check that the post was persisted.

Updating an embed crashes if the post was deleted

When an existing TopicEmbed is found, the update path uses embed.post without verifying that the post still exists. If the embedded topic or post has been deleted, embed.post is nil and PostRevisor.new(post) will raise. Feed polling or retrieval for that URL will then repeatedly fail.

content_sha1 is updated even if the revision fails

TopicEmbed.import updates embed.content_sha1 immediately after calling PostRevisor#revise!, without checking whether the revision succeeded. If the post cannot be saved, the stored SHA1 will no longer match the post contents, and future legitimate content changes may be skipped because the embed record believes it is already up to date.

URL absolutizer mishandles protocol-relative and relative URLs

absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src values that start with '/'. Protocol-relative URLs such as '//cdn.example.com/x' are also matched and incorrectly rewritten to the current host, and ordinary relative URLs such as 'page.html' are left unchanged. This can break links and images in imported content.

PostCreator accepts arbitrary cook_method without validation

PostCreator now assigns post.cook_method from @opts[:cook_method] without validating the value or restricting which callers may use raw_html. Since the raw_html cook method bypasses the normal sanitization pipeline, exposing or forwarding this option accidentally could allow unsafe HTML to be stored.

Embed iframe URL assumes discourseUrl has a trailing slash

embed.js builds the iframe src as discourseUrl + 'embed/best?...'. If discourseUrl is provided without a trailing slash, the resulting URL becomes invalid, for example 'https://forum.example.comembed/best'. The script should normalize discourseUrl or insert a slash when missing.

The embed script calls comments.appendChild(iframe) after document.getElementById('discourse-comments'). If the host page does not contain an element with id discourse-comments, comments is null and the script throws a TypeError, preventing any further script execution.

Migration uses force: true and can drop existing data

CreateTopicEmbeds creates the topic_embeds table with force: true. In a migration this will drop the table if it already exists, destroying any existing topic embed records. Migrations should not use force: true unless intentional data loss is explicitly desired.

Unrelated migration changed to force table recreation

This PR modifies the existing create_top_topics migration to use force: true. That change is unrelated to embed handling and can drop an existing top_topics table, losing data if the table already exists in an environment where this migration is applied or reapplied.

Feed fetch has no timeouts

PollFeed uses open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without configuring connect/read timeouts. A slow or unresponsive feed can hang the job and occupy a Sidekiq worker indefinitely.

The spec expects TopicRetriever to be instantiated and retrieve directly, but EmbedController#best enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic instead. The test therefore does not verify the actual behavior of the controller unless jobs are executed inline, and it does not assert the job arguments.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

Existing callers using downsize(from, to, width, height) will now have height interpreted as opts, or will raise ArgumentError if an options hash is also supplied. The controller passes dimensions='80%' to OptimizedImage.downsize. For animated GIFs, OptimizedImage uses gifsicle --resize-fit #{dimensions}, and gifsicle expects WIDTHxHEIGHT rather than a percentage. The command will fail, so large animated GIFs will not be downsized and the loop will either retry uselessly or proceed with an oversized file.

FileHelper.download was changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a fixed 10.megabytes for all URL-based API uploads. This ignores both max_image_size_kb and any attachment size limit, allowing the server to download up to 10MB even when the configured limit is lower.

The loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) and ignores the return value. If the conversion or optimization fails, truncates the file, or produces a corrupt image, the original uploaded data has already been overwritten and the controller may continue to Upload.create_for with a damaged or zero-byte file. The condition uses FileHelper.is_image?(filename), which treats SVG as an image elsewhere in Discourse. OptimizedImage.downsize is a raster ImageMagick resize and cannot meaningfully or safely reduce an SVG file in place. Large SVG uploads will repeatedly fail downsizing or may be corrupted before upload; vector formats should be excluded or handled separately.

There are no tests for the new server-side downsizing loop, including oversized images, failed conversions, animated GIFs, SVGs, or interaction with configured size limits. These cases are likely to regress and are risky areas of this change.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists

TopicsController#unsubscribe does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then dereferences `tu.notification_level`. For users without an existing topic_users row for the topic, `tu` is nil and the action raises NoMethodError. The action should create or update the row, for example via TopicUser.change or find_or_create_by.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same nil dereference: when no TopicUser record exists, tu is nil and accessing its methods causes a crash.

State-changing unsubscribe action is a GET route without CSRF/token

The unsubscribe action changes TopicUser.notification_level in response to a GET request and skips XHR checks. Rails CSRF protection does not apply to GET, so any logged-in user visiting a malicious page could have topics silently muted or downgraded by an image or link to /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe. Email unsubscribe links should use a signed one-time key or a POST route.

The unsubscribe action mutates notification_level with `tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change`. This skips setting notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id and does not publish the MessageBus level-change event. Leaving notifications_reason_id nil can allow later automatic tracking to override the user's mute, and open clients will not receive the state change.

The `unsubscribe_link` translation was changed to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but Email::MessageBuilder only has that value when the caller passes `unsubscribe_url`. Any other email or plugin that builds with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but omits `unsubscribe_url` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send.

track_visit! uses topic id as user_id when passed ids

In `TopicUser.track_visit!`, `user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic` falls back to the `topic` argument rather than the `user` argument when the second argument is not a User object. TopicsController calls this with integer topic_id/user_id, so it can create or update topic_users rows with user_id equal to the topic_id, corrupting per-user topic state. The fallback should be `user`.

Spec does not assert the new unsubscribe_url is included

The updated spec passes `unsubscribe_url` to Email::MessageBuilder but only asserts that the body contains `user_preferences_url`. It never checks that the new per-topic unsubscribe URL appears in the body or HTML, so the new interpolation/link behavior is untested.

true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same issue: throwing a generic Error for an authentication or authorization failure causes tRPC to report an internal server error instead of a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code such as FORBIDDEN.

true_positives.golden_comment: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

The cache last-updated timestamp is formatted using Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US') regardless of the user's locale. This ignores localized date preferences and can show an English/US-formatted timestamp to non-English users.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same localization bug: formatting the date with hardcoded 'en-US' instead of the user's locale, resulting in potentially incorrect date representation.

false_positives.candidate:
Delete-cache mutation does not refresh connected calendars

The deleteCache mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback. It does not invalidate or refetch viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike the disconnect mutation. Since SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper displays cache status from that query and may not provide an onChanged handler that invalidates it, the UI can keep showing the old cache status and timestamp after cache deletion succeeds.

getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns the maximum updatedAt for CalendarCache rows without filtering by expiresAt, while getCachedAvailability only treats rows with expiresAt >= now as valid. As a result, connectedCalendars can report cacheUpdatedAt and show cache actions for credentials whose cache entries are expired, misleading users about whether valid cached data exists.

The wrapper computes shouldDisableConnectionModification as isDisabled || disableConnectionModification, but ConnectedCalendarList receives only disableConnectionModification. When disabledScope matches the current scope, calendar switches are disabled, but CredentialActionsDropdown can still allow deleting cache or disconnecting the integration, defeating the disabled-scope restriction.

The actions prop always renders a fixed-width div around CredentialActionsDropdown. When the dropdown returns null, such as for delegation credentials with no cache or when connection modification is disabled, the empty container remains and creates unnecessary blank space in the list item or alert action area.

dev:cron uses npx tsx without declaring tsx

The dev:cron script was changed to npx tsx cron-tester.ts, but tsx is not listed as a devDependency. npx may download or prompt to install tsx at runtime, making the script network-dependent and less reproducible across environments.

There are no automated tests for the new deleteCache handler's ownership check, the cache deletion behavior, or the connectedCalendars cache-status enrichment. These paths affect authorization and user-visible data, and regressions could go unnoticed without coverage.

This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hours end boundary uses slot start time

The variable end is calculated from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime. The check therefore ignores the event duration when validating the end of working hours. A slot that starts inside working hours but ends after endTime will pass, potentially offering slots beyond a host's working hours.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: the end time is calculated using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, causing working-hours validation to ignore the slot's actual end.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

Dayjs objects are compared with strict equality

The check comparing date.start and date.end uses === between two Dayjs objects. This compares object identity, not timestamp, so it is always false. The intended handling of a zero-length override where start equals end never triggers. Use .isSame() instead.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify strict equality between Dayjs objects as comparing references rather than date values, causing the equality check to fail, and recommend using .isSame() instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Date override short-circuits busy-time check

In checkIfIsAvailable, when a date override exists for the day, the function returns true before running the busy.every overlap check. Any calendar busy time or existing booking during the override is ignored, so slots can be offered even though the host is busy. This can cause double bookings, especially for fixed hosts whose availability must block the whole event.

Date override validation allows partially overlapping slots

The override exclusion only tests whether the slot ends before the override starts or starts after the override ends. It does not test whether the slot starts before the override or ends after it. Therefore a slot that only partially overlaps the override is treated as inside it. For fixed hosts, a slot such as 09:30-10:30 can pass even if the host override is only 10:00-11:00.

Working-hours check accepts slots when no working hours cover the day

The new workingHours validation only rejects a slot if it finds a workingHours entry for the slot weekday and the slot is outside that entry. If the host has no workingHours entry for that weekday, or workingHours is empty, find returns undefined and the host is treated as available subject only to busy times. This allows fixed hosts to be booked on days they have no scheduled availability.

Multiple date overrides on the same day make valid slots unavailable

The date override loop marks the slot as outside if it is outside any override on that date. If a user has two overrides on the same day, a slot inside one override is outside the other, causing dateOverrides.find to return true and checkIfIsAvailable to return false. The logic should accept a slot if it is contained in at least one override.

Multiple working-hour intervals are handled incorrectly

workingHours.find returns true when the slot is outside any single working-hours interval. If a user has split working hours, such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, a valid slot in one interval is outside the other, so the slot is rejected. The code should accept a slot if it fits in at least one interval.

Date override date matching is not done in UTC

dayjs(date.start).add(...) creates a local-mode Dayjs, while slotStartTime is explicitly UTC. The YYYY MM DD comparison therefore depends on the server's local timezone and can mismatch near date boundaries. The adjusted override times should be constructed in UTC before formatting and comparing.

Timezone-converted overrides can wrap to another day without handling

After applying the invitee/organizer offset, start and end minutes are derived from hour() and minute(), which wrap at midnight. If the timezone conversion moves an override into the previous or next local day, the code still assigns those minutes to the current invitee day, which can drop the override or place slots on the wrong day. Converted ranges that cross midnight need to be split or filtered by the resulting date.

Missing tests for fixed-host round-robin override behavior

The added test only checks a personal event with a different attendee timezone. The PR description says it fixes round-robin events with fixed hosts and date overrides, but there is no test asserting that a fixed host's date override restricts round-robin slots, nor that busy times inside an override remain unavailable. Those regressions are not covered.

In the catch block, the retryCount update is not protected from failure. If the reminder was deleted concurrently or the update otherwise fails, the update error masks the original scheduling error and aborts processing of the remaining reminders. Using updateMany or wrapping the retry-count update in its own try/catch would make the cron job more resilient.

In AuthzClientCryptoProvider's ECDSA converter, integerToBytes truncates any BigInteger whose byte array is longer than qLength by copying only the last qLength bytes. For a valid ECDSA signature, r and s must not be larger than the coordinate size, allowing at most one leading zero byte. Silently truncating oversized DER integers accepts malformed signatures and changes the numeric value, which can create signature malleability or unexpected verification behavior. The method should reject values that do not fit and should also reject negative integers.

ASN1Decoder.readSequence does not validate that the declared SEQUENCE length is exactly consumed. If a child TLV is longer than the remaining sequence length, the remaining length becomes negative and parsing stops without error. If trailing bytes exist after the SEQUENCE, they are ignored because asn1derToConcatenatedRS only reads the first sequence. This lenient DER parsing can accept malformed or appended signature bytes. It should reject non-zero remaining length, child lengths that exceed the sequence, and unconsumed trailing input.

ECDSAAlgorithmTest generates a default EC key pair and only asserts that concatenated R/S bytes are stable across conversion. It does not initialize the generator with the curves associated with ES256, ES384, and ES512, does not verify the reconstructed DER signature with the public key, and does not cover edge cases such as r/s values with the high bit set, leading zeros, extreme values, or malformed DER. TotalDocs iterates cache map without locking

TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu, while BuildIndex mutates the same map under cacheMu. This is a concurrent map read/write race that can panic or return incorrect document counts, especially now that index builds are more concurrent.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug. TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization while BuildIndex writes to the map concurrently, which can cause a concurrent map read/write panic. The candidate does not mention the specific call site near the watcher goroutine, but the underlying issue is identical.

false_positives.candidate:
Data race in search init worker pool

In searchSupport.init, totalBatchesIndexed is incremented inside errgroup.Go closures that run concurrently, and the same closures assign to the outer err variable when calling s.build. Neither variable is protected by a mutex or atomic, so this is a data race. The trace/metric count can be wrong and concurrent writes to err can produce undefined error handling.

Watch pump cannot be stopped and can panic on closed channel

The event pump started in searchSupport.init receives from events without checking whether the channel is closed and uses context.Background rather than a cancellable server context. If the storage backend closes the event channel during shutdown, the loop receives nil values indefinitely and handleEvent will dereference a nil *WrittenEvent. The goroutine also cannot be stopped by server shutdown.

Initial index build can miss writes that happen during startup

searchSupport.init builds all indexes first and only then calls storage.WatchWriteEvents. The resource versions returned by build are discarded, so mutations that occur while an index is being built, and before the watch starts, are neither included in the initial build nor replayed from the watch. This can leave the search index stale for affected resources until another mutation happens for that resource.

Existing Bleve index is replaced without being closed

BuildIndex stores the newly created index in b.cache[key] without closing any previous index for that key. If a concurrent or repeated build replaces an existing entry, the old Bleve index remains open, leaking memory/file handles and potentially holding directory locks.

File-backed BuildIndex may reuse stale documents from previous runs

For file-backed indexes, bleve.New(dir, mapper) opens an existing Bleve directory if present. BuildIndex then writes current documents but never removes documents that no longer exist, for example resources deleted while the process was stopped. Unless the directory is ephemeral, stale/deleted resources can remain searchable after restart.

Nil IndexMetrics can panic in handleEvent

handleEvent increments and decrements IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds without checking whether IndexMetrics is nil, while other call sites guard for nil. If metrics are not initialized, processing an ADDED or DELETED watch event will panic.

Nil IndexMetrics can panic in Bleve BuildIndex

BuildIndex increments resource.IndexMetrics.IndexTenants without checking whether resource.IndexMetrics is nil. Since other code treats IndexMetrics as optional, this can panic during index creation when metrics are not initialized.

DocCount error can skip Flush and fail the whole build

index.DocCount is called only for metrics/logging, but its error overwrites err and then prevents index.Flush from running and causes the build to fail. A doc-count failure should not abort index creation or skip flushing; use a separate error variable for DocCount.

No cleanup when NewResourceServer initialization fails

NewResourceServer calls s.Init(ctx) and returns immediately on error without calling cancel or Stop. If initialization partially succeeded before the failure, for example lifecycle hooks ran or the search watch started, the constructed server's context and goroutines/resources are leaked.

History and Origin can nil-pointer panic when search is disabled

History and Origin call s.search.History and s.search.Origin without checking whether s.search is nil. NewResourceServer can create a server with search disabled, so these gRPC methods will nil-pointer panic instead of returning a not-configured error like Search does.

Postgres integration test is skipped

The postgres integration test is now skipped, removing coverage for a supported database path at the same time startup initialization behavior changes. Postgres-specific regressions may go undetected unless this skip is tracked and temporary.

false_positives.candidate:
Cycle suppression is integration-wide rather than scoped to the originating external issue

Invalid assignment source dict silently disables cycle protection

`AssignmentSource.from_dict` returns `None` when parsing fails, and `sync_assignee_outbound` then proceeds as if no assignment source existed. If a non-empty assignment source dictionary is malformed, missing required fields, or contains unexpected fields due to serialization or version skew, the same-integration cycle protection is silently lost and the outbound sync may propagate back to the originating integration. At minimum, log or emit a metric when a provided assignment source cannot be parsed; alternatively make parsing tolerant of unknown fields while still validating required ones.

Missing suppression test for deassign with a matching assignment source

The PR adds a test showing that `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` with a matching `AssignmentSource` suppresses outbound sync, but there is no equivalent test for `GroupAssignee.objects.deassign`. false_positives.candidate:
Uses Python 3.13-only queue shutdown APIs

OrderedQueueWorker catches queue.ShutDown (also at line 142) and FixedQueuePool.shutdown calls Queue.shutdown(immediate=False) at line 238. queue.ShutDown and Queue.shutdown were added in Python 3.13. If this consumer runs on an older Python interpreter supported by Sentry, attribute resolution or the shutdown call will fail at runtime, breaking worker exception handling and/or graceful shutdown. This needs a compatibility fallback or an explicit Python 3.13+ requirement.

Strategy.close shuts down a shared queue pool that may be reused after rebalance

ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool per factory (result_consumer.py line 133) and passes that same pool to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy (result_consumer.py line 254). SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close shuts down the pool. Arroyo can close a strategy on partition revocation/rebalance and later create a new strategy from the same factory. After the first close, the pool's queues and worker threads are permanently shut down, so later submissions will fail and be treated as completed, allowing unprocessed messages to be committed.

Shutdown does not drain queues and can drop pending work

FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown = True before draining queues, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join/close never waits for wait_until_empty. Workers therefore stop after their current item, leaving queued WorkItems unprocessed. OrderedQueueWorker also never calls work_queue.task_done(), so any shutdown/join path that depends on unfinished tasks cannot complete correctly. On consumer shutdown, queued messages can be discarded and completed offsets may not be committed.

OffsetTracker iterates all_offsets keys while other threads mutate it

get_committable_offsets builds list(self.all_offsets.keys()) without a global lock while submit()/add_offset() can concurrently insert new Partition keys. This can raise RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration. The commit loop catches the exception, but that iteration's commits are skipped, which can delay offset commits during partition churn.

Work queues are unbounded, providing no backpressure

FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize and submit() uses put() unconditionally. If workers are slower than incoming Kafka messages (for example due to a slow subscription), the consumer will continue polling and queueing decoded WorkItems without bound, retaining both decoded results and original messages. This can exhaust memory; the claimed 'natural backpressure' does not exist.

Offsets are completed even when processing fails

OrderedQueueWorker calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in a finally block even when result_processor raises. ResultProcessor.__call__ also swallows handling exceptions. Therefore a message that fails handling (for example a transient DB error) is treated as done and becomes committable. The consumer will commit past it and never retry it, despite the strategy's documentation saying offsets are committed only after successful processing.

submit() marks failed submissions as completed, allowing unprocessed offsets to commit

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit catches all exceptions and, when broker metadata is present, adds and immediately completes the offset. If queue_pool.submit fails (for example because the queue is shut down, the pool is in a bad state, or an unexpected error occurs before enqueue), the message is never processed but is still considered complete, so the commit loop may commit it and silently lose the result.

Committable-offset calculation scans integer ranges and sets repeatedly

Every commit-loop iteration computes min(all_offsets) and max(all_offsets) for each partition and then loops over every integer from start to max_offset. With large batches, many outstanding offsets, or a stuck offset, this can become CPU-intensive. The per-partition offset sets also grow until a contiguous prefix can be committed, increasing memory pressure during backlogs.

join() ignores its timeout and does not flush pending work

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join(timeout) simply calls close(), which stops the commit thread with a fixed 5-second join and shuts down the pool without waiting for queued items or honoring the supplied timeout. Arroyo's join contract is to allow pending processing to finish up to the timeout; this implementation can terminate early and leave work unprocessed/uncommitted.

Hash-distribution test is nondeterministic

test_different_groups_distributed asserts that 20 hashed group names hit all three queues. Python's randomized string hashing does not guarantee that every bucket is hit for this small sample, so the test can fail intermittently. It should use a deterministic hash function or only assert consistent assignment.

Negative --max-workers creates an invalid queue pool

For thread-queue-parallel mode, num_queues is set to max_workers or 20. A negative max_workers value is truthy, so FixedQueuePool receives a negative num_queues; range(num_queues) creates no queues and hash(group_key) % negative_num_queues can produce invalid indices. The CLI option should validate that max_workers is positive.
